annotations.description: MiniMx Sarge is casting Echo of Eons for its full mana cost of {4}{U}{U} (6 mana), which requires sacrificing Lotus Petal and likely cracking both LEDs. However, the much better line is to cast Chrome Mox first (imprinting one Echo of Eons), then sacrifice both LEDs (discarding the remaining Echo of Eons to hand along with anything else), generating 6 mana, and then cast Echo of Eons from the graveyard for its flashback cost of {2}{U} — which only costs 3 mana. This approach preserves more permanents on the battlefield (Chrome Mox stays, potentially one or both LEDs could be re-used via sequencing) and puts Sarge in a much stronger position post-Echo. By casting Echo at full cost first, Sarge wastes resources and ends up with fewer permanents after the reshuffle. Additionally, the opponent has Goblin Welder on board, so giving the opponent a fresh 7 cards while Sarge has fewer permanents is risky. The sequencing of Chrome Mox first, then LED cracks to enable flashback Echo, is strictly superior.

annotations.description: The opponent has Painter's Servant on the battlefield, which makes all cards share a color. With Grindstone resolving onto the battlefield, the opponent can activate Grindstone to mill MiniMx Sarge's entire library and win the game. MiniMx Sarge had Veil of Summer available to cast, which would grant hexproof from blue and black — but more critically, the opponent has Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast in the graveyard (not relevant) and Goblin Welder tapped. The key issue is that Veil of Summer should have been cast here instead of Dark Ritual. With Painter's Servant making everything blue (among other colors), Veil of Summer would: (1) draw a card since the opponent has cast blue spells, (2) make MiniMx Sarge and their permanents hexproof from blue, which would prevent Grindstone from targeting them (since with Painter's Servant, Grindstone's activation targets a player, and that player would have hexproof from blue — but actually Grindstone targets 'target player' not with a color restriction). Wait — Veil of Summer grants hexproof from blue and black. Grindstone says '{3}, {T}: Target player mills two cards.' Grindstone is colorless but with Painter's Servant it's also the chosen color. If the chosen color is blue, then Grindstone would be a blue permanent, and its ability would be a blue ability. With Veil of Summer giving hexproof from blue, MiniMx Sarge couldn't be targeted by Grindstone's ability. This is the critical defensive play — Veil of Summer would prevent the Painter-Grindstone combo from targeting them. By casting Dark Ritual instead, MiniMx Sarge allowed Grindstone to resolve and left themselves vulnerable to the combo kill.

annotations.description: GPT41m Analyst already has the Painter's Servant + Grindstone combo assembled on the battlefield. Goblin Engineer's ETB ability lets you search YOUR library for an artifact and put it into YOUR graveyard - it doesn't let you interact with opponent's artifacts. The player chose Lion's Eye Diamond which belongs to MiniMx Sarge, but Goblin Engineer's ETB searches your own library, not the battlefield. However, looking more carefully at the choices presented, these appear to be artifacts on the battlefield that Goblin Engineer can target with its activated ability (not the ETB). Wait - the stack shows Goblin Engineer is resolving, and the ETB says 'you may search your library for an artifact card, put it into your graveyard, then shuffle.' So this must be a different trigger or the game is presenting battlefield artifacts for some reason. Actually, re-reading: the message says 'Select an artifact' with choices including battlefield artifacts from both players. This seems to be Goblin Engineer's activated ability ({R}, {T}, Sacrifice an artifact: Return target artifact card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield) - but Engineer just entered so it has summoning sickness and can't tap. More likely this IS the ETB and the interface is showing artifacts incorrectly, or it's asking which artifact to sacrifice. In any case, the critical issue is that the player has Painter's Servant and Grindstone on the battlefield - they should be activating Grindstone to win the game immediately (pay 3, tap Grindstone targeting opponent). With Painter's Servant naming a color, all cards share that color, so Grindstone mills the entire library. Instead of winning the game, the player is fiddling with Goblin Engineer. If they must resolve this ETB, they should search their own library for something useful, not pick an opponent's artifact. But the real blunder is not recognizing they can win this turn with the combo already assembled.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Grindstone targeting MiniMx Sarge (paying 3 mana from Mountains) to mill their entire library with Painter's Servant on the battlefield, winning the game. For the Engineer ETB, search library for a useful artifact backup like a Lotus Petal or similar.

annotations.description: MiniMx Sarge has the opportunity to respond to Mishra's Research Desk resolving (it's on the stack via Unearth) by casting Brainstorm (U available from Mox Opal... wait, Mox Opal is tapped). Actually, looking more carefully: all lands and Mox Opal are tapped, but there are two Lion's Eye Diamonds untapped. The player could crack LED for UUU (discarding hand) in response to the Research Desk being on the stack, then cast Brainstorm with U floating. But wait - LED discards hand, so Brainstorm would draw 3 and put 2 back with no hand otherwise. More importantly, the player has Dark Ritual and Brainstorm as options listed. Looking at the choices: Brainstorm {U}, Dark Ritual {B}, Dark Ritual {B} are all castable, meaning there must be untapped mana sources. But the board shows all lands and Mox Opal tapped. The choices being available suggests LED can be cracked. Actually, the game engine is offering these as legal plays, so mana must be available somehow. The player declined all responses, letting the Research Desk resolve, giving the opponent access to exile cards. Casting Brainstorm here would let the player dig for answers and set up the top of their library, which is significant when they have Echo of Eons in the graveyard and could potentially combo. Declining to use Brainstorm at instant speed (end of opponent's turn or in response) when it's available is a missed opportunity, though the reasoning 'took 3 damage from something' is confused and irrelevant.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Brainstorm to dig for combo pieces or answers. With Echo of Eons in graveyard and LED on board, finding the right pieces could enable a combo turn. At minimum, Brainstorm at instant speed is almost always correct when you have the mana and want to improve your hand before your own turn.

The reasoning 'Opponent keeps passing back' is nonsensical - it's MiniMx Sarge's main phase and they should be advancing their game plan.
